scenario: Ridge run. 4 miles of exposed ridge ahead.
Sky's clear overhead, but you just heard thunder.
realityCheck: If you can hear thunder, you're within striking distance. An exposed ridge is the worst place to be when it arrives.
headline: Clear sky. Distant thunder.
caption:
Blue sky above, thunder somewhere behind you.

Comment SEND or BAIL.

scenario: Summit is 1.2 miles and 900 ft away.
Sunset in 60 minutes. Headlamp at 15%. 5 miles back to the car.
realityCheck: Descents in the dark run far slower than you plan for, and 15% won't last.
headline: 60 minutes of light. 15% battery.
caption: Summit is right there. So is sunset. Comment SEND or BAIL.

scenario: 34°F. Mile 3 of 12.
The creek is calf deep and there's no log.
headline: 34 degrees. Calf-deep creek.
caption:
9 miles left either way.

Comment ON or OFF.

scenario: Last pitch. A passing shower just soaked the rock.
Anchor is 40 ft up. Your partner is getting cold.
realityCheck: Friction drops a lot on wet rock. Know your retreat before you need it.
headline: 40 feet. Wet rock.
caption: So close. So slick. Comment SEND or BAIL.

scenario: 18 inches fell overnight. Danger is Considerable on NE aspects.
Your line faces NE. There are already tracks in it.
realityCheck: Tracks don't mean a slope is stable, and many avalanche accidents happen at Considerable.
headline: Fresh tracks. Considerable danger.
caption:
Someone else already skied it.

Comment SEND or BAIL.

scenario: New trail. A drop that looks rollable.
You can't see the landing. Your friends already went.
headline: Can't see the landing.
caption: Everyone else made it. Probably. Comment SEND or WALK.

scenario: 5 miles from the car, the trail splits.
Your GPS says left. The trail sign says right.
headline: The GPS and the sign disagree.
caption:
One of them is wrong.

Comment GPS or SIGN.

scenario: 14 miles into a group run. The pace has been too fast all day.
Someone says, "Let's add the extra loop."
headline: "Let's add the extra loop."
caption: There's always one. Comment SEND or NOT.

scenario: Mile 40 of a 50-miler. Next aid station is 5 miles away.
Cutoff in 55 minutes. Your legs are cooked.
headline: 5 miles. 55 minutes.
caption:
Chase the cutoff or call it?

Comment SEND or BAIL.

scenario: 80°F. 6 miles to the car. Half a liter left.
There's a stream right here. No filter.
realityCheck: Waterborne illness is real but usually delayed and treatable. Serious dehydration in heat is the more immediate risk. A backup tablet fixes all of this.
headline: Half a liter. 6 miles. 80 degrees.
caption: Thirsty math. Comment DRINK or HOLD.

scenario: The summit cairn is half a mile away.
A whiteout is rolling in, and your tracks behind you are filling.
realityCheck: In a whiteout, your own tracks are often the best way home.
headline: Half a mile. Tracks disappearing.
caption: Tag the summit or follow your tracks? Comment SEND or BAIL.

scenario: Descent. The trail switchbacks 2 miles down to the car.
A loose scree gully cuts straight there in 0.4.
headline: 2 miles of switchbacks. Or 0.4 of scree.
caption:
Your knees have opinions.

Comment SCREE or TRAIL.

scenario: A hard snowfield crosses the trail. 200 ft across, rocks at the bottom.
No microspikes. The detour around adds 45 minutes.
realityCheck: A slip on firm snow picks up speed fast, and the runout is what decides how it ends. Without traction, the detour is the honest call.
headline: 200 feet of firm snow. No spikes.
caption:
45 minutes or one committed shuffle.

Comment CROSS or AROUND.

scenario: Day two. Planned camp is 4 miles and 1,400 ft away.
You're wrecked. There's a flat spot with water right here.
headline: 4 more miles. Or right here.
caption: Tomorrow-you is watching. Comment PUSH or STOP.

scenario: The col is 700 ft above you. Wind just picked up hard.
Your partner's hands are already numb. Car is 3 miles back.
realityCheck: Wind strips heat faster than cold air alone, and numb hands are an early sign, not a late one. Turning around is a decision you can make while you can still make decisions.
headline: 700 feet. Numb hands.
caption:
The col is right there. So is the wind.

Comment SEND or BAIL.

scenario: Fork in the singletrack. Left is the blue you know.
Right is a new black with a sign that says "Expert. No bailouts."
headline: Blue you know. Black you don't.
caption:
The sign is doing a lot of work.

Comment BLACK or BLUE.

scenario: Mile 9 of a 14 mile loop. Headlamp is in the car.
Sunset is in 50 minutes and the back half is slower.
headline: 5 miles. 50 minutes of light.
caption:
Finish the loop or cut back the way you came?

Comment SEND or BAIL.

scenario: Forecast says 28°F tonight. Your sleeping bag is rated to 40.
Trailhead is 6 miles back. Camp is 2 miles ahead.
realityCheck: A 40 degree bag at 28 degrees is a long night, not an emergency, if you have dry layers and a decent pad. Without them, it can become one.
headline: 28 degrees. A 40 degree bag.
caption:
Every layer you own, or every mile back to the car.

Comment CAMP or OUT.

scenario: Two pitches up a four pitch route. Clouds building fast.
The last two are the easiest. Rapping now means leaving gear.
realityCheck: Easy pitches still take time, and a wet rappel is harder than a dry one. Gear is cheaper than the alternative.
headline: Two pitches left. Clouds building.
caption:
Easy climbing ahead. Weather behind.

Comment SEND or BAIL.

scenario: Fog came in. The cairns stop here.
Your map says the trail bends left along the cliff edge. Your gut says right, through the boulders.
realityCheck: In fog, a map and compass beat instinct nearly every time. Cliff edges are exactly where people's guts get it wrong.
headline: Fog. The cairns stop here.
caption:
Map says one thing. Gut says another.

Comment MAP or GUT.

scenario: Mile 18 of a 26 mile trail race. You're on pace for a PR.
Your running partner is cramping badly and asks you to stay.
headline: PR pace. Partner cramping.
caption:
Eight miles to decide what kind of runner you are.

Comment STAY or GO.

scenario: Lake crossing, 1 mile of open water to the takeout.
Whitecaps just started. Hugging the shore adds 4 miles.
realityCheck: Cold water and wind build faster than they look from shore, and a swim a half mile out is a different problem than a swim near it. The long way is the paddle you'll remember fondly.
headline: 1 mile of open water. Whitecaps.
caption:
Straight across or hug the shore?

Comment SEND or BAIL.

scenario: Trail climbs into a cold rain. Your shell is in the car, 2 miles back.
Summit is 1.5 miles and 1,100 ft ahead. You have a fleece.
realityCheck: Wet fleece at altitude in wind is how most hypothermia cases start, and they start in the 40s, not below freezing.
headline: Cold rain. No shell.
caption:
A fleece and some optimism.

Comment SEND or BAIL.

scenario: The ridge narrows to a knife edge for 200 ft. Exposure on both sides.
A ledge system below looks like it bypasses it. Looks like.
headline: Knife edge. Or the ledge.
caption:
Known exposure or unknown bypass?

Comment RIDGE or LEDGE.

scenario: First storm of the season. 10 inches on bare rock and grass.
Your favorite early line is in. So are the stumps under it.
realityCheck: Early season snow hides what it doesn't cover. Most October ski injuries are impacts, not avalanches.
headline: First storm. 10 inches on rock.
caption:
The line is in. So is everything under it.

Comment SEND or BAIL.

scenario: Mile 2 of 10. Your shoe just blew out at the toe.
Car is right there. You have duct tape and a sock.
headline: Blown shoe. Mile 2. Duct tape.
caption:
Eight more miles on tape and faith.

Comment TAPE or CALL.

scenario: Creek crossing, thigh deep, moving fast after yesterday's rain.
Camp is on the other side. Upstream is a bridge, 3 miles round trip.
realityCheck: Thigh deep and fast is where crossings go wrong. Water pushes much harder than it looks, and a pack makes it worse. Three miles is cheap.
headline: Thigh deep. Moving fast.
caption:
Camp is 60 feet away. Across that.

Comment CROSS or BRIDGE.

scenario: Summit is 0.3 miles away. You've been moving for 9 hours.
Last bus from the trailhead leaves in 2 hours. It's 4 miles down.
headline: 0.3 miles up. Last bus in 2 hours.
caption:
Twenty minutes to the top. Maybe.

Comment SEND or BAIL.
